matchups.name: broodscale bloodchief
matchups.stance_rationale: Force of Vigor, Boseiju's channel, and Dismember attack their engine pieces (Soul-Guide Lantern, Urza's Saga, Vexing Bauble, Basking Broodscale) without taxing our own cascade density or graveyard plan. Damping Matrix does NOT symmetrically shut our own Cycling/Channel/loot suite: per CR 109.2, 'Activated abilities of artifacts and creatures' (with no zone stated) scopes to permanents on the battlefield, and per CR 702.29a cycling functions only from a player's hand, where a creature card is not a 'creature' under CR 109.2 -- Street Wraith, Curator of Mysteries, Generous Ent, Oliphaunt, Colossal Skyturtle, and Waker of Waves are untouched, and Boseiju, Who Endures is a Legendary Land Damping Matrix never mentions at all. Damping Matrix is boarded in here, replacing Tormod's Crypt, because it is a free answer to their own non-mana activated abilities -- Soul-Guide Lantern's 'Sacrifice: Exile each opponent's graveyard' and Haywire Mite -- at zero cost to our plan, while Tormod's Crypt is moved to the reanimator-shaped matchups where its instant-speed graveyard exile actually fizzles a spell on the stack; the in/out totals are unchanged because it is a straight swap.

Nature's Claim ('Destroy target artifact or enchantment', 100% of pulled sideboards) does answer it -- a clean one-for-one on a lock piece they have to answer, not a blank -- while the Urza's-Saga-fetched Haywire Mite that would otherwise exile it works through '{G}, Sacrifice this creature: Exile target noncreature artifact or noncreature enchantment', an activated creature ability a resolved Matrix has already shut off. Once resolved it shuts Soul-Guide Lantern's '{T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Exile each opponent's graveyard' (100% main, the one card here that beats Living End outright), Urza's Saga chapter II and Haywire Mite (all activated, non-mana abilities of permanents, CR 109.2) at zero cost to our own cycling, which functions only from hand (CR 702.29a)

Destroy up to two target artifacts and/or enchantments,' which is a free, off-turn, permanent answer to all four of this matchup's hardest sideboard cards at once -- Vexing Bauble (artifact), and High Noon / Blood Moon / Rest in Peace (all enchantments per resolve_cards' type_line). The boros-aggro-dossier calls High Noon 'the single most dangerous card in their 75' since it stops the cascade combo outright (CR 601.3 + CR 702.85a) and states 'Boseiju, Who Endures is the only maindeck answer' -- a single copy, sorcery-speed, one-shot. Force of Vigor is a second, redundant, instant-speed, free answer to that same card, plus a hard answer to Goblin Bombardment. The two Sink into Stupor are the correct cut to make room: they were a one-shot bounce on Voice of Victory/Ranger-Captain of Eos/Goblin Bombardment (per the playbook's interaction table), but Anger of the Gods already exiles those same toughness-3-or-less bodies outright once it is in the 75, so Sink into Stupor's creature-removal job is now redundant with Anger of the Gods while Force of Vigor covers a job (permanent artifact/enchantment removal) nothing else in this configuration does. Damping Matrix is removed from this matchup: it is now boarded in for broodscale bloodchief and creatures toolbox instead, where its target (a non-mana activated ability of an opposing artifact/creature) is a bigger share of what beats us than Ranger-Captain of Eos's sacrifice ability is here, and High Noon's static lock (which Damping Matrix never touched) is still answered by Force of Vigor's redundant free removal.

Damping Matrix is a counter and NOT a symmetric_counter: CR 109.2 makes 'artifacts and creatures' with no zone named mean permanents on the battlefield, CR 403.3 confirms permanents exist only there, so a Street Wraith, Generous Ent or Oliphaunt being cycled from HAND is a creature card, not a creature, and pays nothing. It is a partial answer, not a lock: Devoted Druid's '{T}: Add {G}' is a mana ability and survives, Badgermole Cub's and Leyline of Abundance's 'whenever you tap a creature for mana' clauses are triggered abilities and survive, and Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler's '+1: Untap up to one target creature' is a planeswalker loyalty ability Damping Matrix never mentions - a 4-of in 10 of 10 lists, so they keep one untap a turn whatever we resolve. Note on this row's opponent: `creatures toolbox` and `devoted combo` are the same deck under two archetype ids the source never merged (c22029ff-3de2-424e-85bc-c270daf9558a and c4fc27b7-4e36-4b08-a070-4d5824a6d1a6). Ten recent top-8 lists per label carry an identical 28-card four-of core - 4 Badgermole Cub, 4 Delighted Halfling, 4 Devoted Druid, 4 Green Sun's Zenith, 4 Nature's Rhythm, 4 Leyline of Abundance, 4 Tyvar, Jubilant Brawler - in 20 of 20, plus 2 Birds of Paradise in 20 of 20. The two labels are temporally disjoint: statistics_decks returns zero `creatures toolbox` decks dated on or after 2026-08-13 and zero `devoted combo` decks dated on or before 2026-08-10, overlapping only on 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-12. This is a relabel, not a fork, so `creatures toolbox` is the retired label and its card reads are frozen at 2026-08-12. The shares do NOT double-count: `shares` partitions 100pp over deck counts at 0.074683pp per deck, so 43 decks + 44 decks = 87 decks = 6.4974pp is this deck's true single share, and a slot serving both rows is credited once for each half of it. What the split does cost is ranking - each half reads as the field's #8/#9 matchup when the merged deck is its #3, behind instant reanimator (7.8417) and broodscale bloodchief (6.6468) - and it costs currency, because the live card reads come from the 44 recent `devoted combo` lists only.

free, off-turn removal for up to two artifacts and/or enchantments (resolve_cards: 'Destroy up to two target artifacts and/or enchantments'; the alternative cost exiles a green card instead of paying mana) -- answers Vexing Bauble, Leyline of Abundance, Blood Moon, Amulet of Vigor, Urza's Saga, esper control's four maindeck Relic of Progenitus, maindeck Tormod's Crypt, and 45c aggro's Scion of Draco (an artifact creature) or Leyline Binding/Leyline of the Guildpact (both enchantments) across 11 matchups without taxing our own cascade (mv4). The third copy is one of the two slots freed by cutting Foundation Breaker: it covers every matchup Foundation Breaker covered, and unlike Foundation Breaker it is free and it is instant speed.

a {2}{U} counter (resolve_cards: mana_cost {2}{U}, mana value 3) whose text 'This spell costs {2} less to cast if it targets a blue spell' drops it to {U} against nearly every relevant spell in the eleven matchups that board it. At mana value 3 each copy sits exactly on the Violent Outburst / Shardless Agent cascade floor -- the same treatment Anger of the Gods gets elsewhere in this board -- so it is never a cascade collision; Tormod's Crypt (mv0) is the only true sub-mv3 collision this board carries. A fourth copy was rejected this pass on slot economy, not cascade math: the 15-card board is already 3 Dismember + 3 Force of Vigor + 3 Mystical Dispute + 2 Damping Matrix + 2 Tormod's Crypt + 2 Anger of the Gods = 15/15, so a fourth Dispute can only be added by cutting one of the other five cards, each of which answers matchups Dispute does not.

a static {3} artifact reading 'Activated abilities of artifacts and creatures can't be activated unless they're mana abilities'. It is a COUNTER, not a symmetric_counter: CR 109.2 scopes an unzoned card-type description to permanents, CR 403.3 confirms permanents exist only on the battlefield, so our own cycling and channel abilities activated from hand are untouched. Answers Devoted Druid's untap, Soul-Guide Lantern, Urza's Saga chapter II, Haywire Mite, The Stone Brain, Walking Ballista, Agatha's Soul Cauldron and Fiend Artisan across 3 matchups now that urzatron has left the field.

instant-speed free graveyard exile that can fizzle a reanimation spell on the stack, which is what the four reanimator-shaped matchups it serves are decided by. Mana value 0 makes it the worst cascade collision in the board, and `matchups/creatures-toolbox.json` pitfall #4 names it as exactly that -- it is boarded only where exiling a graveyard at instant speed beats that cost.

a {1}{R}{R} sweeper that deals 3 damage to each creature and exiles what it kills, which is what makes it the answer to the three recursive-creature aggro decks and to hollow one specifically. Mana value 3 sits exactly on the cascade floor, so it is never a cascade collision.

deck_tech.name: Which cycler goes first
deck_tech.quirk: They are not interchangeable: only one is free, and two of them fetch a land while they fill the graveyard.

lines.why: Cycling costs two life and no mana, so it is the only cycler that does not compete with holding up Force of Negation. Against a turn-three kill that is the whole difference.

lines.mode: Ent or Oliphaunt for a surveil land
lines.why: Forestcycling and Mountaincycling reach Hedge Maze, Commercial District and Thundering Falls, whose surveil puts a second card in the yard. They enter tapped, so it costs the turn.

lines.mode: Ent or Oliphaunt for an untapped shock
lines.why: Breeding Pool, Stomping Ground and Steam Vents all carry a basic type. Against a turn-four clock the untapped land is worth more than the extra graveyard card.

lines.mode: Waker of Waves to dig, not as a beater
lines.why: One mana looks at two cards, puts one in hand and bins the other: a cycle and a Living End target at once. Sequence it early rather than keeping it to hard-cast.

deck_tech.name: Sink into Stupor: land or spell
deck_tech.quirk: Every copy is a land drop we might need and the only maindeck answer to a permanent that has already resolved.

lines.mode: as Soporific Springs, paying three life
lines.why: A tapped land loses the turn that matters against a turn-four clock. Three life is cheap next to missing the cascade turn by one.
Bouncing a resolved Primeval Titan or an Eldrazi is the only maindeck answer we have once their enters trigger has already happened.
When the cascade turn is still a turn away the land drop is not urgent, and three life against a deck with any reach is real.

deck_tech.name: Cascade turn, free spells, or no Living End at all
deck_tech.quirk: Living End has no mana cost and can only be cascaded into, so the question is whether this matchup wants it cast at all.

lines.why: Bait the counter with the first cascade spell, then resolve the second behind Force of Negation. Their clock is slow enough that a setup-heavy keep is still a keep.

lines.mode: free spells as the whole plan
lines.why: The evoke and pitch suite works with no mana at all, so Subtlety and Endurance beat a ramp deck that never gets a turn where its mana is the problem.
Living End returns their graveyard too. Against a deck filling its own yard it is a wrath in their favour, so the cyclers already on board are the clock.

meta_calls.why: A third Crypt fizzles Persist, Unearth or Goryo's Vengeance on the stack with the spell still on the stack, free and at instant speed, in the extra reanimation-shaped matchup this field now carries.
meta_calls.cost: Down to one Anger of the Gods, so boros aggro, boros energy, hollow one and ur cutter prowess each lose a copy of the sweeper their fast starts are answered by.

meta_calls.why: Damping Matrix stops the Broodscale loop without answering a creature, which is the only angle that survives their Cage and Jailer.
meta_calls.cost: Down to one Crypt, so Reanimator, instant reanimator, esper goryo and the mirror each lose an answer - and the Crypt is what wins the mirror's split.

meta_calls.why: Consign counters the cascade trigger itself, and Force of Negation only answers spells. Dispute costs one against a blue spell and taxes Consign three they do not have open.
meta_calls.cost: One fewer graveyard answer against Reanimator and against the mirror, where the Crypt is the card that wins the split.

gaps.why: We still run no removal that kills their real threats. Quantum Riddler is 4/6 and a delved Murktide Regent is routinely 7/7 or larger, so the third Dismember boarded here (-5/-5) kills neither; what it actually answers is Harbinger of the Seas, Psychic Frog and Orcish Bowmasters. This is a structural gap, not an oversight: Temur has no instant-speed removal for a 6-toughness flier at mana value 3 or above, and anything below mana value 3 is a live cascade collision under Violent Outburst and Shardless Agent. If the cascade turn is denied twice - a pre-emptive Thoughtseize, then a counter on the second attempt - the matchup becomes a card-quality grind this removal-light shell is not built to win. At 2.5034pp (statistics_archetypes, modern: dimir control 29 decks + dimir control 26 decks) this sits mid-field, behind esper blink (5.2344pp), eldrazi ramp (5.0523pp), broodscale bloodchief (4.9613pp), devoted combo (4.8248pp), instant reanimator (4.4151pp), boros aggro (3.0041pp), living end (2.9131pp), ur cutter prowess (2.6855pp) and pinnacle affinity (2.6400pp) - not the second-largest matchup in the field.

Force of Despair (resolve_cards: 'If it's not your turn, you may exile a black card from your hand rather than pay this spell's mana cost. Destroy all creatures that entered this turn.') is a free, one-sided blowout on our own Living End turn specifically, timed to resolve after our creatures have already entered; nothing in the 75 protects a just-resolved board from it, and the only recourse is a second Living End or a fast enough clock that they never draw it.
